COR-TRY-23-030, Quarterly Summary of Tenders/Quotations and Request for Proposals Approved by the Chief Administrative Officer
Strategic Priority - Equitable Services and Opportunities
COR-FFC-23-006, 134 Frederick Street, Kitchener
notes:
Craig Dyer, Commissioner of Corporate Services and Chief Financial Officer, discussed the report, offering an overview and outlining the next steps. He explained that the property will undergo additional assessment and recommendations will be presented to the Council by late 2024 or early 2025.

Responding to questions from the Committee, Bruce Lauckner, Chief Administrative Officer, explained that staff will engage in further discussions with the City of Kitchener regarding 134 Frederick Street, Kitchener. He elaborated on the current process, highlighting that, in accordance with Regional policy, Regional staff are prioritizing internal Regional services and will expand to other municipal services if Regional options are unavailable.

In response to a Committee question, Jerry Biersteker, Director of Facilities and Fleet Management, mentioned that the estimated property value as of 2021 is around $10 million. C. Dyer added that the assessment process will consider various factors, including determining the most suitable use for the building, identifying Regional applications that align with the location, and conducting cost analysis for renovations and future operations. This comprehensive work is planned to be completed over the next year or so.

B. Lauckner, acknowledged the Committee's direction and confirmed that staff would return with potential location options for a future Indigenous hub.

items.title: COR-FFM-23-007, Update on the Former Kinsmen Children’s Centre - 651 Concession Road, Cambridge
notes:
J. Biersteker spoke to the report and provided an update on the Former Kinsmen Children’s Centre - 651 Concession Road, Cambridge, sharing next steps which included the Committee's endorsement on the recommendations with the uses identified, that Regional staff would engage with the City of Cambridge staff to assess the concept's suitability for that location, proceed with applying for study grants, and return to Council in 2024 with a detailed redevelopment proposal and an updated cost estimate for approval.

In response to questions from the Committee, J. Biersteker mentioned the potential for this to serve as supportive housing. C. Dyer then offered additional details regarding provincial cost-sharing, specifically in the context of using it as a paramedic facility. He explained that the province does not directly subsidize capital investments but does provide a 50% subsidy on the asset's amortization.

Addressing a question from the Committee, Sarah Miller, Manager of the Land Portfolio, discussed the road's accessibility, noting that it's situated on an active bus route. Additionally, Concession Road is a Regional road, ensuring the presence of sidewalks within its right of way and adjacent walkways leading to the nearby school site.

items.title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion
notes:
Councillor C. Huinink introduced her motion noting that this motion deals specifically with the surplus, not the police budget itself. She further noted that everyone benefits from the police services and that it is a service that we all need. 

In response to a question from the Committee, Graham Walsh, Regional Solicitor indicated that staff can seek opinions on a technical issue such as this, and will look beyond internal resources if that is the direction of the Committee. 

The Committee agreed to defer the motion until November 7, 2023 to allow for a staff report, legal opinion, and comment from Waterloo Region Police Services.

Responding to a question from the Committee, C. Dyer provided insight into the interaction between Regional staff and police services and the budget preparation process from a financial standpoint. He clarified that continuous discussions occur between the Region's staff and the Waterloo Region Police Services regarding budget assembly. While many aspects of the budget are determined by the police, staff engagement is required for factors like employee benefits, debt servicing costs, capital program review, and project timing. After Regional staff receive initial budget estimates from the police, these estimates are incorporated into the overall Regional budget.

motions.item_title: COR-FFM-23-007, Update on the Former Kinsmen Children’s Centre - 651 Concession Road, Cambridge
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the Regionally-owned property located at 651 Concession Road, Cambridge (former Kinsmen Children’s Centre) as set out in report COR-FFM-23-007 dated October 10, 2023: Direct staff to explore, in consultation with necessary Regional departments and City staff, the concept of redeveloping the Regionally-owned property located at 651 Concession Road, Cambridge with a Regional multi-use building, including Paramedic Services, affordable housing, and potentially other integrated social service offerings; and Direct staff to proceed with applying for a Federation of Canadian Municipalities Sustainable Affordable Housing study grant for this property.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the Regionally-owned property located at 651 Concession Road, Cambridge (former Kinsmen Children’s Centre) as set out in report COR-FFM-23-007 dated October 10, 2023:

  1. Direct staff to explore, in consultation with necessary Regional departments and City staff, the concept of redeveloping the Regionally-owned property located at 651 Concession Road, Cambridge with a Regional multi-use building, including Paramedic Services, affordable housing, and potentially other integrated social service offerings; and
  2. Direct staff to proceed with applying for a Federation of Canadian Municipalities Sustainable Affordable Housing study grant for this property.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. Huinink Notice of Motion
motions.text: Whereas the Region is facing yet another difficult budget year; And Whereas housing, homelessness, drug addiction and mental health services continue to need additional resources; And Whereas all operating departments of the Region do not retain any surplus that has been able to be achieved; And Whereas the Waterloo Region Police Service in the recent years has been approved to transfer 100% of its surpluses to its own reserve funds; Therefore, Be It Resolved that any future surpluses be retained 50% to WRPS reserve funds and 50% returned to the Region.
motions.text_html:
Whereas the Region is facing yet another difficult budget year;

And Whereas housing, homelessness, drug addiction and mental health services continue to need additional resources;

And Whereas all operating departments of the Region do not retain any surplus that has been able to be achieved;

And Whereas the Waterloo Region Police Service in the recent years has been approved to transfer 100% of its surpluses to its own reserve funds;

Therefore, Be It Resolved that any future surpluses be retained 50% to WRPS reserve funds and 50% returned to the Region.
